properties.subtitle: West Bank
properties.claim: The Star of Bethlehem — moving ahead of the magi, then stopping over one building — is read as a craft under intelligent control, since no astronomical body behaves that way.
properties.context: Astronomical candidates include the 7 BC triple conjunction of Jupiter and Saturn in Pisces and a 5 BC Chinese-recorded nova. The 'stopping' is also readable as retrograde motion, or as Matthew's literary device: the account is shaped to fulfil Numbers 24:17 and appears in only one gospel.
properties.summary: Bethlehem is a city in the West Bank, Palestine, located about ten kilometres (six miles) south of Jerusalem, and the capital of the Bethlehem Governorate. It had a population of 28,591 people, as of 2017. The city's economy is strongly linked to tourism, especially during the Christmas period, when Christians embark on a pilgrimage to the Church of the Nativity, which is revered as the location of the birth of Jesus.
properties.short_description: City in the West Bank, Palestine
